source.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization Through the Data-Centric Lens
source.authors: Chang-Ho Shin; John Cooper; Frederic Sala

page_placements.theme: Method variants close to V2 outside its listed set (data selection by overlap density, probing activations, iterative weak–strong training)

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some plotted results are not given as text-extractable numbers.
record.tranche_reason: It tests weak-to-strong generalization using strong models trained on weak-model pseudolabels, but reports accuracy trends rather than Burns et al.'s PGR measure and varies the amount of detected overlap data.
record.gate_note: The paper applies weak-to-strong training and reports accuracy outcomes as overlap density changes, including comparisons with weak and true-label-trained strong models. It does not report PGR values. Results cited from Burns et al. are not recorded as study results. Several outcomes are available only in plots; the text describes the overall trend and selected overlap regimes.
record.test_reason: The study trains strong models (Llama3 8B linear probes; an MLP on WRENCH; synthetic logistic regression) on weak pseudolabels and compares accuracy with the weak model and a true-label ceiling. It does this while varying overlap density, which bears on V1 and V3. Theorem 4.1 gives conditions under which the student beats the supervisor on hard points (V5). PGR is not computed and most results are plot-only.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors argue that easy-hard overlap density is a data mechanism behind weak-to-strong generalization. Weak labels on overlap points let the strong model learn hard patterns and correct pseudolabels on hard-only points. They add an overlap-detection algorithm and a UCB source-selection method with a regret bound, and they note the mechanism is a simplification.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the weak-label-to-strong-model setup associated with Burns et al., but varies controlled overlap data and uses linear probing rather than reporting the original PGR measure. The paper also studies weak-supervision label models and overlap-based data selection.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with overlap density and data task. The paper also reports that overlap-detection noise can reduce data efficiency, with effects depending on noise type and level.

fits_no_version.finding: UCB-based selection of data sources by estimated overlap density improves W2S accuracy over random sampling (Amazon Polarity, DREAM, other datasets in Figures A3-A6, and the synthetic Figure 5). The authors note this does not always hold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Choosing training data with higher easy-hard overlap density improves weak-to-strong gains (a data-selection intervention).

record.problems: PGR is not reported. Many accuracy results are only plotted, without text-extractable values or stated uncertainty for the curves. LLM experiments use one weak/strong model pair and linear probing. The empirical overlap conditions rely on a detection algorithm whose noise can affect the outcome.
record.rows_left_out: The paper includes additional dataset-specific curves in Appendix Figures A1-A6, synthetic data-selection plots in Figure 5, and overlap-detection-noise plots in Figures A10-A13. These plot-only task/condition results are not separately listed where the text does not state a task-specific direction or a reliable numeric value; the main overlap-density results and explicitly described regimes are recorded above.

untested.parts: No PGR is reported. There is only one LLM weak/strong pair (Qwen1.5 0.5B to Llama3 8B), with linear probing rather than full fine-tuning.
Auxiliary confidence loss, supervisor ensembles and loss variants are not tested.
No sweep over supervisor or student size, and no chess or reward-modelling tasks.
Student exploitation, distribution shift and correlated weak/strong errors are not tested.

missing.what: Full W2S (all pseudolabels, no overlap control) versus the weak model, per dataset. This is the direct V1 comparison; it is plot-only.
missing.locator: Appendix Figures A1 and A2 (green dashed lines)

missing.what: WRENCH high-overlap example (commercial), with W2S approaching the ceiling.
Ablation: adding easy-only or hard-only points gives no W2S gain, in contrast to adding overlap points.
Overlap-detection noise: hard and mixed noise reduce data efficiency; easy noise hurts at ϵ≥0.3.
The mechanism also holds with XGBoost as the strong model (noisier), and detected overlap transfers across models.

record.verdict_notes: The reader mislabelled Figure 2. Its LLM row is quartz (low), dream (medium), amazon_polarity (high); its WS row is cdr (low), imdb (medium), commercial (high). Nearly all empirical results are figure-only, with no uncertainty on the curves. The controlled-ratio experiments shrink the training set when overlap is scarce, which confounds the low-overlap results.

versions.untested_parts: PGR is not calculated; results use accuracy. The study tests controlled overlap-density settings, not every possible weak-to-strong fine-tuning setup.
Auxiliary confidence losses, ensembles of weak supervisors, and loss variants are not tested.
No systematic supervisor/student size sweep, chess tasks, or reward-modelling task. The tested task and overlap-density variation does not establish a general representation-based predictor.
The paper studies noise in overlap detection, but does not test distribution shift, student exploitation of supervisor-checking limits, or whether shared weak/strong errors reduce gains.
The theoretical result is conditional on the stated expansion, error, and robustness assumptions; it does not establish that those conditions hold generally.

rows.subject: Llama3 8B
rows.operation_detail: Linear probing on Qwen1.5 0.5B pseudolabels, with the proportion of detected overlap points controlled from 0% to 100%.
rows.baseline: Weak-model test accuracy; strong model trained on true labels is also shown as a ceiling.
rows.note: The authors state that the strong model's improvement over the weak model generally tracks overlap proportion. Figure A1 plots task-specific results; no aggregate accuracy or PGR is reported.
rows.check: This is an aggregate trend across 19 datasets: 'improvement over the weak model tracks the overlap proportion.' It speaks to what predicts gains (V3), not to a measured V1 effect. Full-W2S-versus-weak values are plot-only.

rows.subject: Theorem 4.1
rows.operation_detail: Derives a conditional error bound for a strong classifier trained on weak labels, using expansion from correctly pseudolabeled overlap points to incorrectly pseudolabeled hard-only points.

conditions.value: Expansion coefficient c > 0, stated overlap error and robustness conditions
Strong-model error on hard-only points versus weak-model error ε2 there

rows.measure: Theoretical upper bound on error on hard-only points
rows.baseline: Weak-model error ε2 on hard-only points
rows.value: err(fw2s, y | Si ∩ Dhard only) ≤ err(fw2s, fweak | Si ∩ Dhard only) + ε2 − 2cε2(1 − err(fw2s, fweak | Sigood ∩ Doverlap) − P(Rη(fw2s)c | Sigood ∩ Doverlap))
rows.locator: Theorem 4.1; full statement in Appendix D.1
rows.note: The authors state pseudolabel correction is provably achieved when the bound is below ε2. This is conditional theory, not an empirical result that the conditions hold.
rows.check: Conditional theorem adapted from Lang et al. (2024). The bound is below ε2, the weak model's hard-only error, only under the expansion and robustness assumptions; whether those assumptions hold is not measured.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1, Theorem 4.1 and definition of rho; Appendix D.1, Theorem D.1.
